The dismissal says "Nothing grew by appending a restatement." But Config.jl:23 reads "The ECONOMY MODEL is the cheaper AI model the tool's model catalogue names (`Preflight.economy_model`)", and Preflight.jl:501 repeats it: "The economy model: the cheaper AI model the tool's model catalogue names...". Both lines came in 47db044, whose message says the model "is defined in Config's map and on economy_model". Config's docstring grew 162->227 words and was re-baselined, although the scan's own message says "rewrite, do not append".
verdicts.what_would_bite: The Config module docstring and Preflight.economy_model's docstring each define the economy model in full, though the Config map already links to economy_model. The 47db044 re-baseline recorded that duplicate as the ratchet's new ceiling, so the ratchet can no longer flag it. If catalog/models.toml's economy entry or the anchor semantics change, one definition can drift from the other. Demote.jl is similar: its docstring was patched in 2026-09-09-check-docs-01, in 2026-09-11-check-docs-01 and twice in this round, and grew 192->234 words. RULE.DOC.SHAPE says a docstring patched three or more rounds "is rewritten whole rather than appended to again", yet it was extended and re-baselined.

verdicts.what_would_bite: The dismissal's premise, "every re-baseline in this window carries its reason; nothing grew by appending", is false for commit 249b795. That commit re-baselined with no reason in the commit and absorbed an appended clause into demote's docstring. Fix passes in three rounds (7503a84, c8ef916, 47db044) had already edited that docstring, and docs-rubric.md says such a docstring is "rewritten whole rather than appended to again". The ratchet (src/Scans/prose_shape.jl:113) now holds the new ceiling, so this growth passes SCAN.PROSE_SHAPE silently from now on.
